title: Mactan: Whose Decision?
imageAlt: Three distinct positions: Magellan demanded recognition of Spain and Humabon; Lapulapu refused; other leaders made different choices. No single decision represents every community.
content:
In the last mission, you learned that a meeting or agreement in Cebu did not decide the future of every island. Now investigate Mactan, near Cebu. Your task is to explain a conflict using evidence.

Lapulapu was a leader of Mactan. The NHCP Mactan marker records that he refused to recognize the king of Spain and the position claimed for Rajah Humabon over Cebu and Mactan. Magellan sought that recognition. This was a disagreement about authority: who could give orders and expect others to obey.

Not all local leaders chose the same response. Zula, another leader in Mactan, sought Magellan's support against Lapulapu. Naming different choices helps us avoid describing all residents as if they had one opinion.

Read the decision cards. Separate a demand from consent: asking people to accept a ruler does not show that they agreed. Use the clues to explain Lapulapu's refusal without inventing a speech or claiming he spoke for a modern nation-state.
clues: A demand
Magellan sought recognition of the Spanish king and Humabon's authority. A demand is not evidence of agreement.
A refusal
The NHCP marker identifies Lapulapu as a leader who refused this recognition.
More than one choice
Zula and Lapulapu did not take the same position. One leader's action cannot represent everyone.
task: Which explanation best fits the disagreement over authority?
Lapulapu refused the authority demanded by Magellan; local leaders made different choices
Every local leader had already accepted the same ruler
Magellan's demand proved everyone consented
A meeting in Cebu made decisions for all islands
reason: The disagreement concerned authority. Lapulapu refused the demanded recognition, while other leaders made different choices.
definition: The power to make decisions and expect others to follow them.

title: Trace the Cause of the Conflict
imageAlt: A cause chain links demands for authority, refusal and an armed attempt to enforce the demand. The chain explains escalation, not an unavoidable outcome.
content:
A cause helps explain why something happened. To understand a battle, go beyond remembering its date. Ask which decisions brought people into conflict.

Magellan joined local disputes and attempted to enforce demands for obedience. The NHCP marker also records that he ordered Buaya burned after its refusal to recognize authority. This was coercion: trying to make people obey through force or threats. The harm to a community is part of the history, even when we study it without graphic images.

Watch how to build a cause chain. First, identify the demand about authority. Next, identify the refusal. Then identify the decision to use force. Connect the events without claiming that a refusal automatically makes an attack acceptable or inevitable.

Try a fictional report check. A student writes that a gift exchange caused everyone to agree to foreign rule. Replace that explanation with evidence about the demands, local choices and the armed attempt to impose authority. Explaining violence is different from praising it.
clues: Name the issue
The dispute involved demands for obedience and recognition, not simply the presence of unfamiliar visitors.
Identify coercion
Threats and force were used to try to make communities obey. That is different from a freely accepted agreement.
Connect decisions
Refusal was followed by an armed attempt to enforce demands. Explaining this sequence does not make an attack justified.
task: Which cause chain explains the conflict most carefully?
Demands for authority met refusal, and Magellan attempted to enforce them by force
A gift exchange proved universal consent, so no disagreement existed
All local leaders chose exactly the same response
A battle happened only because the place had a particular name
reason: Demands, refusal and the decision to use force help explain the conflict. An explanation does not justify coercion.
definition: Trying to make someone obey by using force or threats.

title: Read the Shoreline Clue
imageAlt: Conceptual side view: boats remain offshore, shallow water and coral lie between them and the beach. The diagram has no exact distances, troop positions or scale.
content:
Place can affect what people are able to do. A shoreline is not just a background picture. It can change how boats approach land and how people move.

The National Quincentennial Committee's discussion of Pigafetta's account describes low tide and coral that kept the boats from approaching the beach closely. Magellan's landing party had to cross shallow water. The people defending Mactan confronted that party. These conditions help explain why having ships did not automatically give an advantage on shore.

Read the diagram from the water toward land. Find the boats, the shallow area and the beach. Then connect one feature to a practical effect: boats farther away could not bring people right onto the beach. This is a conceptual diagram, not an exact battle map. It does not supply distances, precise troop positions or everyone's movements.

Use more than one factor in your explanation. Conditions mattered alongside decisions and the defenders' actions. Do not turn one shoreline feature into a rule that predicts the result of every battle.
clues: Look at the water
Low tide and coral limited how closely the boats could approach, according to the account discussed by the NQC.
Connect place and action
The landing party had to cross shallow water rather than step straight from boats onto the beach.
Keep the limit
A simplified shoreline explains a constraint. It does not establish every movement or make one factor the only cause.
task: What does the shoreline evidence help explain?
Boats could not approach closely, affecting how the landing party reached the shore
Ships guaranteed success regardless of local conditions
The diagram gives the exact position of every participant
Coral alone explains every decision and the whole outcome
reason: Shallow water and coral constrained the approach. Conditions mattered alongside decisions and the defenders' actions.
definition: A condition that limits what someone can do.

title: 27 April: Result and Next Steps
imageAlt: Event sequence: battle at Mactan on 27 April 1521; the defenders repelled the attacking party and Magellan died; surviving expedition members continued afterward.
content:
The Battle of Mactan took place on 27 April 1521. The defenders of Mactan defeated the attacking force led by Magellan. Magellan died in the battle. The NHCP marker identifies the warriors of Mactan in this outcome. We can name the result without showing injuries or treating deaths as points in a game.

Separate an immediate outcome from a later event. The immediate outcome concerns what happened at Mactan. Surviving members of the expedition continued the voyage afterward. Magellan's death did not mean that every member of the expedition died or that all later expeditions stopped.

Try sorting a report into three parts: before the battle, the result, and what happened later. Demands and refusals belong before the battle. The attacking party's defeat belongs to the result. Continuing voyages belong afterward.

This victory is remembered as resistance to an attempt to impose authority. It was not the independence of a modern Philippine republic, and it did not end all later attempts to establish colonial rule. The next mission investigates later expeditions.
clues: A specific event
The NHCP Mactan marker dates the battle to 27 April 1521 and records Magellan's death at the hands of Mactan's warriors.
An immediate outcome
Mactan's defenders repelled the attacking party. The result should not be enlarged into a claim about every later event.
A later sequence
Surviving expedition members continued after Mactan. Later voyages still need to be studied.
task: Which statement separates the outcome from later history?
Mactan's defenders won on 27 April 1521; survivors and later expeditions continued afterward
Magellan completed the whole voyage after dying at Mactan
The battle ended every future Spanish expedition
The battle created a modern Philippine republic that day
reason: The defenders won at Mactan and Magellan died. Survivors continued, so this result did not end all later voyages or colonial efforts.
definition: A result of an event or decision.

title: Evidence or Dramatic Retelling?
imageAlt: Three source checks distinguish a participant account, a modern historical marker and an artistic retelling. A dramatic duel or invented speech is not established by an image.
content:
A dramatic picture can help people remember a story. It cannot prove every detail it shows. Historical accounts, modern summaries and artistic retellings are different kinds of material.

Pigafetta took part in the expedition and witnessed the battle. His account is useful evidence, but it gives a participant's viewpoint. The NQC notes that he did not identify Lapulapu among the fighters. We should not turn a familiar picture of a one-on-one duel into a proven event. This uncertainty also does not prove that Lapulapu was absent.

Lapulapu is remembered for leading resistance, and the defenders' collective action mattered. A modern monument can express that memory without being an exact portrait made in 1521. Recognizing leadership does not require inventing a personal duel, exact age or speech.

For this fictional exhibit task, choose a responsible caption. Name the documented event and identify artistic choices as a retelling. Ask what the source supports, whose viewpoint it records, and what remains uncertain. Respectful remembrance includes checking claims.
clues: A participant viewpoint
Pigafetta witnessed the battle. An eyewitness still cannot supply every viewpoint or private thought.
An uncertain detail
The NQC notes that Pigafetta did not identify Lapulapu among the combatants. A personal duel is not established by that account.
A form of remembrance
A monument or modern illustration can honor resistance without establishing an exact appearance, speech or individual action.
task: Which caption treats a dramatic battle picture responsibly?
An artistic retelling of resistance at Mactan; its personal duel is not established by the account
An exact photograph taken during the battle in 1521
Proof of Lapulapu's exact speech and appearance
Proof that one person acted alone without any defenders
reason: Separate evidence from retelling. Lapulapu's leadership and the defenders' victory do not establish a personal duel or exact appearance.
definition: An act of remembering and honoring a person or event.

title: Build Your Mactan Explanation
imageAlt: A report sequence distinguishes causes before the battle, the result on 27 April 1521 and the continuing voyage afterward. It does not claim the chapter is complete.
content:
Complete your investigation by connecting causes, conditions and outcome. Begin with the dispute over authority. Explain that Lapulapu refused recognition and that Magellan attempted to impose demands. Connect a local condition to its effect: shallow water and coral limited the boats' approach. Then state the outcome at Mactan on 27 April 1521.

Use this report frame in your own words: The conflict involved [demand and response]. One condition that mattered was [feature and effect]. The result was [supported outcome]. We should not claim [unsupported detail]. This is a classroom thinking tool, not an original speech.

Before choosing your final explanation, check whether you have made every local leader agree, given credit to one person alone, or treated an artistic duel as proof. Revise any claim that goes beyond the evidence.

Use the mission quiz to check what you learned. If a topic is difficult, revisit its lesson and try targeted practice before another quiz attempt. Passing earns the mission reward once. The reward recognizes learning, not harm. Complete all missions, then pass the chapter challenge to earn the chapter badge.
clues: Explain the cause
Connect a demand about authority, refusal and the decision to enforce it by force.
Connect place and outcome
Explain one constraint without making it the only cause. State the defenders' victory and the continuing history separately.
Check the evidence
Credit collective action, keep uncertain details uncertain, and identify fictional prompts as teaching tools.
task: Which explanation best combines the investigation?
A dispute over authority escalated; local conditions and defenders' actions mattered, and the evidence does not establish a personal duel
One dramatic picture proves everyone's exact words and actions
The boats guaranteed success and every local leader agreed
Mactan's result ended all later expeditions and created a modern republic
reason: A supported explanation connects causes, local conditions and the outcome while keeping uncertain details separate from evidence.
definition: An account connecting events, causes and evidence while stating what remains uncertain.
